nodes.name: Human Approval
nodes.description: Require authorized human approval for consequential actions, high-risk automation, policy exceptions, and irreversible operations.

nodes.name: Separation of Duty
nodes.description: Ensure consequential actions are not defined, approved, executed, and audited by the same actor without independent review.

nodes.name: Approve Contract Review Assistant Deployment

nodes.name: Internet of Agents (survey)

nodes.name: Wikipedia

nodes.name: Agent Collaboration Protocol
nodes.description: Internet-of-Agents collaboration protocol for heterogeneous, distributed agents — registration/discovery, autonomous nested team formation, FSM session control, and structured messaging. Grounded in the IETF IoA Protocol draft.

nodes.name: Agent Identity Protocol
nodes.description: Mutual authentication and attestation of agent and workload identity before any consequential exchange.

nodes.name: Authorization Decision Protocol
nodes.description: Request and receive an authorization decision from a policy decision point, separated from enforcement.

nodes.name: Capability Discovery Protocol
nodes.description: Discover, publish, and verify agent capabilities and packaged artifacts from a governed catalog.

nodes.name: Orchestration Protocol
nodes.description: Agent-as-orchestrator coordination of sub-agents, tasks, and resources toward an objective.

nodes.name: Policy Evaluation Protocol
nodes.description: Evaluate policy-as-code to produce governed, logged policy decisions for agent actions.

nodes.name: Reconciliation Protocol
nodes.description: Agent-as-operator control loop that drives actual state toward declared desired state.

nodes.name: Relationship Authorization Protocol
nodes.description: Check fine-grained relationship-based permissions for scoped agent access.

nodes.name: Agent Memory Poisoning
nodes.description: Risk that malicious or false data is persisted in agent memory to influence future decisions, sessions, or other users (OWASP agentic threat T1).

nodes.name: Agent Tool Misuse
nodes.description: Risk that an agent is manipulated into abusing its integrated tools to perform unintended or destructive actions (OWASP agentic threat T2).

nodes.name: Unauthorized Agent Execution
nodes.description: Risk that an agent performs an action without valid authorization, approval, policy scope, or accountable ownership.

nodes.name: Adverse Selection Mitigation
nodes.description: Address hidden information about agent type via screening, verification, and trust assessment before engagement.

nodes.name: Agency Cost Reduction
nodes.description: Minimize the deviation of agent actions from principal interest and the cost of controlling it.

nodes.name: Commission
nodes.description: Tie compensation to outcomes (e.g. sales) to align agent effort with principal revenue.

nodes.name: Deferred Compensation
nodes.description: Weight reward to later periods to encourage long-term commitment and reveal type over time.

nodes.name: Efficiency Wages
nodes.description: Pay above market to raise the cost of job loss and motivate effort and retention.

nodes.name: Equal Compensation Principle
nodes.description: Value equally-important activities equally so unmonitored tasks are not neglected (avoid multitasking distortion).

nodes.name: Incentive Alignment
nodes.description: Change the rules so the agent's rational self-interest coincides with the principal's intent.

nodes.name: Incentive Intensity Principle
nodes.description: Set incentive strength based on profit sensitivity, measurement precision, agent risk tolerance, and responsiveness.

nodes.name: Information Asymmetry Reduction
nodes.description: Close the knowledge gap between principal and agent through disclosure, traceability, and observability.

nodes.name: Informativeness Principle
nodes.description: Include in the agent's evaluation any signal that reveals information about its effort, filtering exogenous noise.

nodes.name: Monitoring
nodes.description: Reduce information asymmetry by observing agent actions and outcomes at justified cost.

nodes.name: Monitoring Intensity Principle
nodes.description: Match the level of monitoring to the optimal intensity of incentives; monitor more where incentives are strong.

nodes.name: Moral Hazard Mitigation
nodes.description: Detect and deter hidden actions the principal would not approve via monitoring, incentives, and evidence.

nodes.name: Multiple-Principal Resolution
nodes.description: Resolve conflicting objectives when an agent serves several principals (collective-action governance).

nodes.name: Negotiation Delegation
nodes.description: Delegate scoped negotiation authority with a defined reservation price and reputational accountability.

nodes.name: Non-Financial Recognition
nodes.description: Use acknowledgement and praise to raise intrinsic motivation without narrowing the relationship to pure economics.

nodes.name: Objective Performance Evaluation
nodes.description: Assess against explicit, measurable standards; prefer aggregate measures to avoid gaming single metrics.

nodes.name: Piece Rates
nodes.description: Reward measurable output directly to internalize the consequences of effort for simple, repetitive tasks.

nodes.name: Bonding
nodes.description: Have the agent post a bond forfeited on misconduct, giving it skin in the game.

nodes.name: Profit Sharing
nodes.description: Share aggregate output value to align team incentives where individual contribution is hard to isolate.

nodes.name: Promotion-Based Incentives
nodes.description: Use internal advancement as long-horizon pay-for-performance via job and title changes.

nodes.name: Relative Performance Evaluation
nodes.description: Compare an agent to similar peers to remove common shocks and sharpen incentives.

nodes.name: Subjective Performance Evaluation
nodes.description: Use balanced supervisor judgement for complex work; mitigate centrality and leniency bias.

nodes.name: Termination Threat
nodes.description: Use credible threat of ending the relationship to deter shirking and misalignment.

nodes.name: Tournament Incentives
nodes.description: Reward relative rank to motivate effort when absolute measurement is costly; guard against risk-seeking and sabotage.

nodes.name: Trust and Reciprocity
nodes.description: Use repeated interaction and reputation (trust game dynamics) to sustain trustworthy agent behavior.
